| parent = [[Minor International]] | website = {{URL|https://www.minorhotels.com/en|minorhotels.com}} }} '''Minor Hotels''' is an international hotel owner, operator, and investor headquartered in [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]], with more than 550 hotels in over 55 countries across [[Asia–Pacific|Asia-Pacific]], the [[Middle East]], [[Africa]], the [[Indian Ocean]], [[Europe]], and the [[Americas]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.minorhotels.com/en/about-us|title=About Us|website=Minor Hotels|language=en}} Minor Hotels operates as a subsidiary of [[Minor International]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/snapshot.asp?privcapid=111319310|title=Company Overview of Minor Hotel Group Limited|website=Bloomberg}} one of the largest hospitality and leisure companies in the Asia-Pacific region.{{Cite web|url=http://www.austrade.gov.au/invest/investor-updates/2015/thai-hotel-group-invests-in-australias-north|title=Thai Hotel Group Invests in Australias North|website=Austrade}} The group operates hotels under the brands of Anantara Hotels & Resorts, [[Avani Hotels & Resorts]], Elewana Collection, [[Oaks Hotels, Resorts & Suites]], [[NH Hotel Group|NH Hotels]], NH Collection, nhow Hotels, and Tivoli Hotels & Resorts. ==History== American-born Thai businessman [[William Heinecke]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/william-heinecke/|title=William Heinecke|website=Forbes}} founded the hotel group in 1978, with the opening of the Royal Garden Resort Pattaya as its inaugural venture. The property underwent rebranding over the years, initially becoming the Pattaya Marriott Resort & Spa, and is presently known as the Avani Pattaya Resort.{{cite web |url= https://www.travelweekly-asia.com/Travel-News/Hotel-News/A-Minor-change-sees-Marriott-rebrand-to-AVANI-Pattaya |title= A Minor change sees Marriott rebrand to AVANI Pattaya |author= |date= 4 October 2016 |publisher= Travel Weekly Asia |access-date= 11 April 2026 |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260411064351/https://www.travelweekly-asia.com/Travel-News/Hotel-News/A-Minor-change-sees-Marriott-rebrand-to-AVANI-Pattaya |archive-date= 11 April 2026 }} Minor Hotels entered the luxury hospitality market in 2001 with the opening of its first [[Anantara Hotels & Resorts]] in 2001 in [[Hua Hin district|Hua Hin]]. The brand celebrated its 20th anniversary in March 2021, now with a presence in over 40 properties across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, the Indian Ocean, and Europe.{{Cite web|url=http://www.hoteliermiddleeast.com/26370-anantara-marks-15-years-and-its-pipeline-for-2020/|title=Anantara marks 15 years and its pipeline for 2020|website=Hotelier Middle East|date=6 March 2016 }} The hotel group began its expansion into Africa in 2008 by acquiring a 50 percent stake in Elewana Afrika, marking the company's first significant venture into the continent.{{Cite web |date=2011-10-25 |title=Minor takes 50% stake in Elewana Afrika |url=https://www.traveldailymedia.com/minor-takes-50-stake-in-elewana-afrika/ |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=Brand TD |language=en-US}} In 2014, Minor Hotels further solidified its presence in Africa with investments in various properties, enhancing its portfolio in the region.{{Cite web |last=Stephens |first=Matthew |date=2014-08-19 |title=Minor Hotel Group partners with Sun International to strengthen position in Africa |url=https://insights.ehotelier.com/news/2014/08/19/minor-hotel-group-partners-with-sun-international-to-strengthen-position-in-africa/ |access-date=2024-01-29 |language=en-AU}} In 2011, Minor Hotels broadened its portfolio by acquiring [[Oaks Hotels, Resorts & Suites]], a prominent hotel chain based in Australia. The acquisition resulted in Minor Hotels holding a majority stake of 54.3 percent in the hotel chain, extending its reach into the Australian hospitality market.{{Cite web |title=Minor International acquires controlling stake in Australia's Oaks Hotels |url=https://hotelsmag.com/news/minor-international-acquires-controlling-stake-in-australias-oaks-hotels/ |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=HOTELSMag.com |language=en-US}} Minor Hotels expanded in Europe with the acquisition of Tivoli Hotels & Resorts in 2015. This acquisition included 16 properties across Portugal and Brazil, representing its first significant investment in Europe. The transaction was notable for being the largest hospitality deal in Portugal's history.{{Cite web |date=2016-02-02 |title=Minor Hotel Group Completes Largest-Ever Hospitality Deal in Portugal with Acquisition of Tivoli Hotels & Resorts |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/minor-hotel-group-completes-largest-ever-hospitality-deal-in-portugal-with-acquisition-of-tivoli-hotels--resorts-300213612.html |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}} In 2017, Minor Hotels acquired a significant stake in Corbin & King, a hospitality group in the United Kingdom known for notable establishments like [[The Wolseley]] and The Delaunay.{{Cite web |last=Key |first=Alys |date=2017-12-18 |title=Minor Hotels takes £58m stake in The Wolseley and The Delaunay operator Corbin and King |url=https://www.cityam.com/277694-thai-company-minor-hotels-takes-gbp58m-stake-wolseley-and/ |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=CityAM |language=en-GB}} Furthering its investment, Minor Hotels successfully bid to acquire the entire Corbin & King business in April 2022.{{Cite web |last=Hanson |first=Eloise |date=2022-04-01 |title=Minor places winning bid for Corbin & King |url=https://boutiquehotelnews.com/news/industry/minor-bid-corbin-king/ |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=Boutique Hotel News |language=en-GB}} Subsequently, the group was rebranded as The Wolseley Hospitality Group.{{Cite web |last=restaurantonline.co.uk |date=2022-06-09 |title=Minor rebrands Corbin & King as The Wolseley Hospitality Group |url=https://www.restaurantonline.co.uk/Article/2022/06/09/Minor-International-rebrands-Corbin-King-as-The-Wolseley-Hospitality-Group |access-date=2024-01-29 |website=restaurantonline.co.uk |language=en-GB}} Minor Hotels acquired the [[NH Hotel Group]] in 2018. This acquisition added approximately 380 hotels to its portfolio, significantly extending the hotel group's presence in Europe and Latin America.{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/nhhotels-ma-minor-idUSL8N1X6549|title=Minor hotel group secures 94 pct of Spain's NH Hotels|website=Reuters}} ==Brands== ===Anantara Hotels & Resorts=== Anantara Hotels & Resorts, Minor Hotels' luxury flagship brand, was founded in 2001 with its [[Anantara Hua Hin Resort & Spa|first property]] in Hua Hin. Since its inception, Anantara has expanded globally, encompassing properties in diverse locations such as beaches, private islands, countryside retreats, desert sands, heritage sites, and cosmopolitan cities. The brand's portfolio now spans over 40 countries, including [[Austria]], [[Cambodia]], [[China]], [[France]], [[Hungary]], [[Indonesia]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], [[Italy]], [[Malaysia]], [[Maldives]], [[Mauritius]], [[Mozambique]], [[Netherlands]], [[Oman]], [[Portugal]], [[Qatar]], [[Seychelles]], [[Spain]], [[Sri Lanka]], [[Thailand]], [[Tunisia]], [[United Arab Emirates]], [[Vietnam]], and [[Zambia]]. In 2010, the brand launched the Anantara Vacation Club, a points-based timeshare project, offering options in various global destinations. In 2025, Anantara properties in [[Koh Samui]] and [[Phuket]] were used as filming locations for the third season of ''[[The White Lotus]]'', including Anantara Bophut Koh Samui Resort, Anantara Lawana Koh Samui Resort and Anantara Mai Khao Phuket Villas.{{cite web |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/the-white-lotus-real-filming-locations-season-three-thailand-phuket-2025-2 |title=Where was 'The White Lotus' season 3 filmed? |publisher=Business Insider |date=2025-02-15 |access-date=2026-03-09}}{{cite web |url=https://press.wbd.com/na/media-release/hbo-0/white-lotus/white-lotus-s3-shooting-locations |title=The White Lotus S3 Shooting Locations |publisher=Warner Bros. Discovery Pressroom |date=2025-02-11 |access-date=2026-03-09}} ===Avani Hotels & Resorts=== [[Avani Hotels & Resorts]], launched in 2011, currently operates in over 20 countries, including [[Australia]], [[Botswana]], [[Cambodia]], [[Colombia]], [[Italy]], [[Indonesia]], [[South Korea]], [[Laos]], [[Lesotho]], [[Malaysia]], [[Mexico]], [[Mozambique]], [[Namibia]], [[New Zealand]], [[Portugal]], [[Seychelles]], [[Spain]], [[Sri Lanka]], [[Thailand]], [[United Arab Emirates]], [[Vietnam]], and [[Zambia]]. The brand is on a trajectory of growth, with expectations to expand its portfolio to over 100 properties globally by 2026.{{Cite web |last=Ellichipuram |first=Umesh |date=2024-01-29 |title=Minor Hotels plans to open over 200 properties globally by 2026 |url=https://www.hotelmanagement-network.com/news/minor-hotels-globally-2026/ |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=Hotel Management Network |language=en-US}} ===Elewana Collection=== In 2008, Minor Hotels expanded into Africa by acquiring a 50 percent stake in Elewana Afrika, now branded as the Elewana Collection. The Elewana Collection comprises 16 boutique lodges, camps, and hotels across [[Kenya]] and [[Tanzania]], offering unique accommodations. In 2015, Minor Hotels further increased its presence in the region by acquiring a majority stake in four Kenyan properties from Cheli & Peacock, along with associated safari tour operating companies.{{Cite web |title=Minor Hotel Group Continues Strategic Expansion in Africa With Cheli & Peacock's Kenya Portfolio Joining Elewana Collection |url=http://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4070049.html |website=Hospitality Net}} ===Oaks Hotels, Resorts & Suites=== Minor Hotels completed its acquisition of [[Oaks Hotels, Resorts & Suites]], an Australian-based accommodation provider, in 2011.{{Cite web |title=Minor International Takes Oaks Hotels |url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/thai-group-minor-international-takes-oaks-hotels/story-e6frg8zx-1226049433335 |website=The Australian}} The brand, originally founded in Australia in 1991, offers over 60 properties primarily in [[Australia]] and [[New Zealand]], with additional locations in [[China]], [[India]], [[Qatar]], and the [[United Arab Emirates]]. ===NH Hotels=== Minor Hotels acquired a 94.1 percent stake in the Spanish multi-national hotel company [[NH Hotel Group]] during the last quarter of 2018{{Cite web |title=WTM 2018: Anantara parent company acquires 94% stake in NH Hotel Group |url=https://travelweekly.co.uk/articles/315653/wtm-2018-anantara-parent-company-acquires-94-stake-in-nh-hotel-group |website=Travel Weekly}} at a total volume of €2,327m. NH Hotel Group, which includes NH Hotels, NH Collection, and nhow Hotels, operates over 350 hotels in 35 countries. NH Hotels is positioned in the midscale to upscale segment, with urban hotels catering to both business and leisure travelers. ===NH Collection=== Established in 2014, NH Collection operates in the upper to upscale segment, located in major capital cities across Europe and Latin America. ===nhow Hotels=== The hotels are located in urban area. ===Tivoli Hotels & Resorts=== In 2016,{{Cite web|url=http://rciventures.com/news/europe/mhg-completes-portugals-largest-ever-hospitality-deal/|title=MHG Completes Portugals Largest Ever Hospitality Deal|website=RCI Ventures}} Portugal saw its to this Date largest hotel deal when Minor Hotels acquired Tivoli Hotels & Resorts,{{Cite press release|url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/minor-hotel-group-completes-largest-ever-hospitality-deal-in-portugal-with-acquisition-of-tivoli-hotels--resorts-300213612.html|title=Minor Hotel Group Completes Largest-Ever Hospitality Deal in Portugal with Acquisition of Tivoli Hotels & Resorts|website=PR News Wire}} a hotel chain that owns 16 properties across [[Portugal]], [[Brazil]], and [[Qatar]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/thailands-minor-international-to-buys-portugals-tivoli-hotels-and-resorts-1454320984|title=Thailand's Minor International Buys Portugal's Tivoli Hotels and Resorts|website=[[Wall Street Journal]]}} The acquisition, which marked Minor Hotels' entry into Europe and Latin America, totaled €294.2 million.{{Cite web|url=http://rciventures.com/news/europe/mhg-completes-portugals-largest-ever-hospitality-deal/|title=MHG Completes Portugal's Largest Ever Hospitality Deal|website=RCI Ventures}} ==Other ventures== ===Restaurants=== ====The Wolseley Hospitality Group==== Minor Hotels acquired a significant stake in the hospitality group Corbin & King, founded by restaurateurs Jeremy King and Chris Corbin, in 2017. Minor Hotels acquired the entire business in 2022 for £60 million,{{Cite web |date=2022-04-01 |title=New future for London's The Wolseley as Jeremy King's ownership ends |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/world/uk-news/2022/04/01/new-future-for-londons-the-wolseley-as-jeremy-kings-ownership-ends/ |access-date=2022-04-03 |website=The National |language=en}}{{Cite news |last=Hancock |first=Alice |date=2022-04-01 |title=Corbin & King co-founder loses control of The Wolseley |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/dbcd627b-6405-45dd-8285-e223718e5057 |access-date=2022-04-03}} leading to the rebranding of the group as The Wolseley Hospitality Group. The group includes establishments such as [[The Wolseley]], The Delaunay (and The Delaunay Counter), Brasserie Zédel, Manzi's, Colbert, Fischer's, Café Wolseley, Soutine, and Bellanger. ===Wellness=== Minor Hotels has been active in the wellness sector through collaborations and acquisitions. In 2022, Minor Hotels partnered with [[Bangkok Dusit Medical Services]] to open the BDMS Wellness Clinic at Anantara Riverside Bangkok Resort.{{Cite news |title=BDMS and Minor prep health hub |url=https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/general/2411635/bdms-and-minor-prep-health-hub |access-date=2024-01-30 |work=Bangkok Post |date=11 October 2022 |language=en |last1=Apisitniran |first1=Lamonphet }} ====MSpa International==== Originally a joint venture in 1999, Minor Hotels has fully acquired MSpa International, now operating over 70 spas worldwide under brands like Anantara Spa and AvaniSpa. In 2020, Minor Hotels partnered with Clinique La Prairie to open its first medical spa outside of Europe at The St. Regis Bangkok.{{Cite web |title=Clinique La Prairie announces first business venture in Asia {{!}} spabusiness.com news |url=https://www.spabusiness.com/wellness-news/Clinique-La-Prairie-announces-first-business-venture-in-Asia/344965 |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=www.spabusiness.com/}} ===Cruises=== ====Loy Pela Voyages==== Minor Hotels operates river cruises through Loy Pela Voyages, departing from Anantara Riverside Bangkok Resort. The cruises provide a blend of contemporary and historical experiences along the [[Chao Phraya River]], connecting Bangkok with the historical city of [[Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya (city)|Ayutthaya]].{{Cite web |title=A step back in time: Sailing from Bangkok to Ayutthaya on a luxury cruise boat |url=https://cnaluxury.channelnewsasia.com/experiences/bangkok-cruise-ayutthaya-chao-phraya-loy-river-song-loy-pela-voyages-206016 |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=CNA Luxury |language=en}} ====Mekong Kingdoms==== Launched in 2018 by Minor Hotels, Mekong Kingdoms offers luxury river cruises between Thailand and Laos, including routes from the [[Golden Triangle (Southeast Asia)|Golden Triangle]] to [[Luang Prabang]].{{Cite web |date=2018-01-06 |title=Minor Hotels launches Mekong Kingdoms luxury cruises |url=https://www.tatnews.org/2018/01/minor-hotels-launches-mekong-kingdoms-luxury-cruises/ |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=TAT Newsroom |language=en-US}} ===Trains=== ====The Vietage by Anantara==== The Vietage by Anantara offers luxury train travel in Vietnam, featuring 12-seat carriages, with routes connecting [[Da Nang]], [[Quy Nhon]], and [[Nha Trang]].{{Cite web |title=The Vietage by Anantara Unveils All-New Luxury Railway Journey |url=https://www.hospitalitynet.org/news/4119592.html |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=Hospitality Net |language=en-us}} ==Partnerships== *In early 2021, Minor Hotels formed a strategic partnership with Funyard Hotels & Resorts to expand its presence in China.{{Cite web|url=https://www.hotelbusiness.com/minor-hotels-enters-strategic-partnership-with-funyard-hotels-resorts-for-china-expansion/|title=Minor Hotels Enters Strategic Partnership With Funyard Hotels & Resorts for China Expansion|website=Hotel Business|date=20 January 2021 }} *Minor Hotels formed a partnership with VLCC to develop wellness and beauty centers, starting with Avani+ Hua Hin Resort.{{Cite web|url=http://bwhotelier.businessworld.in/article/VLCC-Ventures-into-Global-Wellness-Tourism-with-Exclusive-Global-Tie-Up/14-10-2019-177498/|title= VLCC Venture Into Global Wellness Tourism With Exclusive Global Tie-Up|website=BW Hotelier}} *Minor Hotels is launching the Asian Institute of Hospitality Management in collaboration with [[Les Roches International School of Hotel extract: Minor Hotels is an international hotel owner, operator, and investor headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand, with more than 550 hotels in over 55 countries across Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, Africa, the Indian Ocean, Europe, and the Americas. Minor Hotels operates as a subsidiary of Minor International, one of the largest hospitality and leisure companies in the Asia-Pacific region. The group operates hotels under the brands of Anantara Hotels & Resorts, Avani Hotels & Resorts, Elewana Collection, Oaks Hotels, Resorts & Suites, NH Hotels, NH Collection, nhow Hotels, and Tivoli Hotels & Resorts.
